diagrams.title: From Vetted Seat to Repeatable High-Ticket Close
diagrams.subtitle: Commission-only closing on $3K-$25K offers over Zoom
diagrams.caption: Closers vet the owner first, win the seat with high-volume outreach, screen applications for cash on hand, run pain-first discovery, and judge results weekly against a 30-40% close-rate floor.
diagrams.assumptions_note: Sequence assembled from practitioner operator gates and pro-tips. Figures are attributed claims, including Cosper's 10% closer, 5% setter, and 15% self-set split with refund clawbacks.
diagrams.note: Sources include Colby Lyman, Frankie Isaac, Hudson Cosper, Scale Like ZK, Daniel Coutts, and Daniel Botero.

stages.label: Vet the Owner and Offer
stages.detail: Ask how many reps there are, what reps make, and how long the program has run, and request case studies (Colby Lyman). Treat fewer than 20 calls a week as a flag (Frankie Isaac). Reject pay-to-apply roles, tickets under 2K, and '10K guaranteed' pitches (Hudson Cosper).

stages.label: Win the Seat With Outreach
stages.detail: Run 100 DMs a day and 60-second Looms. Isaac's student Lucas landed nine interviews from 30 Looms, and another student, Adam, earned $9K in month one.

stages.label: Screen Cash on Hand
stages.detail: Ask about cash on hand in the application. A '$500' answer means cancel the call or offer a low-ticket downsell instead of burning a closer slot (Scale Like ZK).

stages.label: Run Pain-First Discovery
stages.detail: Run 30-45 minute diagnostic calls before any pitch. Probe each objection with what, why, and how, because every objection is a smokescreen (Daniel Coutts).

stages.label: Close and Track Weekly KPIs
stages.detail: Hold a 30-40% close-rate minimum against a 70-80% target on 5-10 calls a day (Hudson Cosper). Check KPIs weekly, because a bad show rate alone can turn $50K into $5K (Scale Like ZK).

diagrams.title: From Yacht Sale Price to Broker Take-Home
diagrams.subtitle: Tiered schedule, co-broker split, and house split
diagrams.caption: A $30M yacht carries a potential $1.75M commission on the tiered schedule. Co-broker and house splits then cut what a single working broker keeps.
diagrams.assumptions_note: Each stage restates a separate practitioner example rather than one continuous deal. The $1M commission is the Yacht Broker Masterclass illustration, and the 60/40 split applies under most circumstances.
diagrams.note: Schedule and $30M example from a Northrop & Johnson broker on Yachts For Sale. Split and take-home figures from Yacht Broker Masterclass.

diagrams.title: The State-Level M&A Broker Relief Gap
diagrams.subtitle: The federal exemption did not preempt the states
diagrams.caption: 23 states adopted M&A-specific relief and Washington's private-placement route adds one more. 26 states plus DC still lack relief, so unregistered fees can become uncollectible.
diagrams.assumptions_note: The starting count is the 50 states plus DC. Coverage counts follow the IBBA BEEF advocacy tally. Adoption came by rule, order, or law.
diagrams.note: Tally from the International Business Brokers Association panel, which also cites a Nevada broker who spent about $500K in legal fees.

diagrams.title: Success-Fee Ranges by Intermediary Type
diagrams.subtitle: Main Street percentages versus sliding ladders on larger deals
diagrams.caption: Main Street brokers charge 10-15% with nothing upfront. M&A advisors slide from 10% down to 2% on the double Lehman, and digital marketplaces taper by deal size.
diagrams.assumptions_note: The typical value is the practitioner's stated example or a stated middle tier, not an average. Ladders apply each rate to a portion of the price.
diagrams.note: Sources are American Business Intermediaries, CompassPointCapital (Nate Grant), Business Broker Crowd Call, Colin Matcha, and Business Solution.

diagrams.title: Four Gates Before Signing an NCNDA
diagrams.subtitle: An NDA stops talking, while non-circumvention stops the deal without you
diagrams.caption: Kill fake ICC paper, confirm real non-circumvention coverage, execute before disclosure, and strike buried non-competes or commission liability.
diagrams.assumptions_note: Gate order follows practitioner operator gates. Term guidance of 2 to 5 years is an IXH TRADING Academy range, and Cangem Global calls 3 years a hard bet.
diagrams.note: Sources are Cangem Global Corporation, IXH TRADING Academy, Trade Base Hub, Dr. Chad Michael Altieri, David C Barnett, and Rafael Ludwig.

nodes.question: Does the paper avoid citing ICC 400, 500, or 600 rules and avoid the IMFPA label?
nodes.fail_action: Treat it as fake and refuse to sign. ICC 769E is the only genuine ICC NCNDA.

nodes.question: Is it a real non-circumvention instrument covering affiliates, survival period, and remedy?
nodes.fail_action: Send it back, because a plain NDA only stops talking.

nodes.question: Have authorized signatories executed it and completed KYC with government photo ID?
nodes.fail_action: Share zero protected names, prices, or shipping details until they have.

nodes.question: Is the term reasonable, with no buried non-compete, buyer commission liability, or advance-fee demand?
nodes.fail_action: Cross out the clause, or walk away from any advance-fee request.

diagrams.title: Price the Paper, Not the Pitch
diagrams.subtitle: Four specialist lanes and the benchmark each one runs on
diagrams.caption: Specialist brokers anchor each lane to a hard benchmark. Examples include close rates and fee ladders for digital businesses, rent multiples for towers, power agreements for land, and IRS risk for credits.
diagrams.assumptions_note: Headcount was not reported by practitioners. Benchmarks are attributed claims, and the tower multiple is a starting point rather than a calculator.
diagrams.note: Sources are The Digital Merchant, Colin Matcha, Tower Genius, Reed Smith LLP, and Andrew Dubinsky.

center.focus: Underwrite documents and benchmarks before the pitch

spokes.kpi: FE International closes 94% of listings; underwrite on at least six months of numbers
16-17x annual rent with a right of first refusal, 17-18x without
Signed power agreement, dated load ramp, and an off ramp before any premium
About 1 in 20,000 invalidation odds, with the buyer carrying the risk

diagrams.title: Supervision and Recordkeeping Cadence
diagrams.subtitle: Inspection cycles and record buckets in years
diagrams.caption: OSJs are inspected annually, while branches run on three-year cycles. Records sit in six-year and three-year buckets, with two years kept easily accessible.
diagrams.assumptions_note: Year counts are the practitioner-cited cycles and record buckets. Rule 1017 separately triggers at 25% of assets or ownership control, filed at least 30 days before the change.
diagrams.note: Sources are The Finance Lab on OSJ inspections and Rule 1017, and Business Broker Crowd Call on licensing context.

buckets.label: OSJ Inspection Cycle
buckets.notes: Mandatory annual inspections once a branch manager gives final new-account approval

buckets.label: Long Record Bucket
buckets.notes: Six-year retention bucket, first two years easily accessible

buckets.label: Short Record Bucket
buckets.notes: Three-year retention bucket, first two years easily accessible

diagrams.title: Building Closing Certainty Before the Buyer Arrives
diagrams.subtitle: Clean books, honest disclosure, binding exclusivity, and protected seller money
diagrams.caption: Closing certainty starts with tax returns that tie to P&Ls and an honest CIM. It continues with 60-to-90-day exclusivity and a seller note carrying offset rights, all run fast enough to beat deal fatigue.
diagrams.assumptions_note: The four-week sequence is an organizing frame, not a practitioner timeline. The reported target close is 3 to 6 months, with fatigue at 4 to 6 months.
diagrams.note: Sources are Charles Weatherly, iGOTHAM, Patrick O'Connell, Quiet Light Brokerage, My SBA Loan Pro Podcast (Jake Parsley), and Amped Success (Mark Sims).

weeks.title: Tie the Books
weeks.deliverable: Three years of tax returns tied to the P&L line by line, with unreceipted add-backs stripped
weeks.gate: No listing goes out until every add-back has a receipt

weeks.title: Disclose and Draft the CIM
weeks.deliverable: Settled suits, state tax matters, and change-of-control leases disclosed in an honest CIM
weeks.gate: No hidden weakness that would surface at week six as broken trust

weeks.title: Lock the LOI
weeks.deliverable: LOI or IOI covering price, terms, and 60 to 90 days of binding exclusivity
weeks.gate: Reject 100% seller-financed full-price LOIs unless it is a partner buyout

weeks.title: Protect the Close
weeks.deliverable: Seller note with an offset right and a data-request turnaround inside the month
weeks.gate: Keep part of the seller's money in the buyer's pocket instead of escrow
